To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the elasticity of the value function of the option with respect to the fuel price is positive, and the value function of option increases as fuel price increases.

(1) microgrids are valuable real option investments, which are worth more than their net present values, (2) microgrids with interdependency between fuel price and cost of technology are more valuable than those with independency, (3) microgrids that can switch between investment and suspension are more valuable than the ones that are either always invested or always suspended, (4) microgrids can be more valuable than the sum of their parts.

the value of the option to invest is greater than the net present value (NPV) of the microgrid investment and that the value of flexibility to suspend and re-activate the microgrid is greater than the NPV of the microgrid.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (i) the closed form contingent analysis for microgrid investment under uncertainty; (ii) the elasticity of option values to prices and its role in closed form contingent analysis; (iii) the optimal switching between investment and suspension and re-activating of investment in microgrid.
a real option approach that can be used to value microgrid assets, taking into account the uncertainties in prices and costs, as well as the flexibility of microgrid operation.
the valuation of a microgrid asset, which is a portfolio of PV, gas-fired and storage assets, and the optimal timing of its investment, suspension and/or re-activation under uncertainty.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the real option approach to investment in renewable energy assets, such as microgrids, can provide a useful and insightful analysis.
real option approach is a better approach for investment in microgrid, as compared to the net present value approach.
the closed form solutions are more accurate than the traditional Black and Scholes (B&S) solutions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
closed form contingent analysis of real options is a viable alternative to simulation-based approaches for the valuation and management of microgrid investments.

the elasticity of option value can be used to determine the sensitivity of the value of the real option to the underlying price processes and that the closed form solutions can be used to analyze the optimal timing of investment, suspension and activation of microgrid assets.

closed form solutions are obtained for the optimal investment decision, which can be used to examine a wide range of scenarios, and that the elasticity parameter can be used to identify the most critical parameters in microgrid investment decision.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the closed form solutions are very accurate in predicting the optimal investment decisions, even when the microgrid load is stochastic, as opposed to deterministic.
a real options approach is a more appropriate framework to analyze microgrid investment under uncertainties, and closed form contingent solutions are useful in that regard.
the closed form solutions are very useful in the analysis of microgrid investment, and that operational flexibility of microgrids can significantly increase the expected net present value.
